intro: The genitive is the fourth case, the case of belonging and of 'of': das Auto des Mannes (the man's car), die Farbe des Hauses, die Tasche der Frau, die Meinung der Leute. Its forms are the smallest set of the four: masculine and neuter take des and add -s or -es to the noun (des Mannes, des Films, des Autos, des Hauses — -es after one syllable or a hissing sound), feminine and plural take der and leave the noun alone (der Frau, der Straße, der Kinder). After ein-words: eines Mannes, einer Frau, meines Bruders. Names simply add -s without an apostrophe: Annas Auto, Peters Buch. In speech the genitive is often replaced by von + dative (das Auto von dem Mann), which is fine — but in writing — newspapers, letters, official notices — the genitive is everywhere, and the prepositions wegen, während and trotz take it. In this quiz you write the whole genitive phrase — article and noun — because the -(e)s on the noun is where most mistakes happen.
tips[0].title: des …-(e)s / der …
tips[0].text: m/n: des Mannes, des Kindes, des Lehrers, des Autos — -es for short nouns and after -s/-ß/-z/-x (des Hauses), -s otherwise. f/Pl: der Frau, der Wohnung, der Leute, der Kinder — no change to the noun.
tips[0].trap: English puts the possessor first ('the man's car'); German puts it after (das Auto des Mannes). Names are the exception: Annas Auto, no apostrophe.
tips[0].check.why: Neuter genitive: des + noun with -s. Zimmer has more than one syllable, so just -s.
tips[0].visual.caption: The fourth row. Masculine and neuter nouns take -s or -es too.
tips[0].visual.rows[0].label: Nom
tips[0].visual.rows[1].label: Gen
tips[1].title: Names: -s, no apostrophe
tips[1].text: Annas Auto, Peters Buch, Frau Müllers Büro. Only names ending in s/z/x take an apostrophe: Hans' Auto, Max' Fahrrad.
tips[1].check.why: Names ending in s, z or x take only an apostrophe in the genitive: Klaus' Auto.
tips[2].title: von + dative in speech
tips[2].text: das Auto von meinem Bruder = das Auto meines Bruders. Both correct; von is casual, the genitive is written and formal. You will read the genitive everywhere; when you speak you may use either.
tips[2].check.why: von takes the dative, and the dative plural of meine is meinen.
tips[3].title: wegen, während, trotz + genitive
tips[3].text: wegen des Wetters (because of the weather), während des Konzerts (during), trotz des Regens (despite). Also (an)statt. In speech: wegen dem Wetter — but careful writing prefers the genitive.
tips[3].check.why: während takes the genitive: masculine des, and the noun adds -s.
remember[1]: wegen – während – trotz take the genitive.
mistakes[0].why: Masculine genitive adds -(e)s to the noun.
mistakes[1].why: German names take -s with no apostrophe.
mistakes[2].why: wegen takes the genitive in written German.
hook: The genitive is how German writes 'the man's car' and 'because of the weather' — small forms you'll see in every newspaper.
